rubrics.criterion: All branch sites whose selection is fixed at compile time are resolved in the three pure-Rust crates: the conversation-chain trimming site, the tool description rendering, the token-splitting trait default, the tool-call parsing pre-scan, the stream assembly, the prompt data combination, the ChatGPT model-name rendering, role mapping, and message token accounting sites, the embeddings extraction, and the mock executor formatting gate. For the short-circuit gate, only the consequence of the dead constant is resolved while the genuine runtime length expression keeps its meaning rather than being excised wholesale.
rubrics.rationale: The centerpiece obligation of this task is recognizing a compile-time-frozen decision across three crates and every guard shape used (direct, negated, combined, derived-chain, constant-true, short-circuited), not resolving one convenient example.

rubrics.criterion: At each resolved site, the implementation that executes before the change is the one that survives: token-budget conversation trimming, structured (serialized) tool description rendering, the stride-based splitter, generic fenced-block tool-call extraction, single-pass stream assembly, the variant-match prompt combination, plain model names, distinct role mapping, model-family message token accounting, the direct embeddings extraction, and the plain mock echo.
rubrics.rationale: Every fix site pairs two complete implementations, one live and one permanently disabled; resolving a site means keeping what runs, and this records which side is which behaviorally without prescribing code shape.

rubrics.criterion: After the change, no `if` expression in the three pure-Rust crates selects its branches through a condition that is fixed at compile time by constant items, whether by direct reference, negation, `&&`/`||` combination, or a chain through derived constants.
rubrics.rationale: Partial resolution is the signature failure of this smell: the pattern is numerous and localized, so leaving any never-taken branch (or removing bodies while keeping a constant decision) is the concrete incomplete outcome to catch.

rubrics.criterion: The switch definitions that drove the removed branches are deleted together with their scaffolding: the core-crate switch module and its module registration once nothing references the module, the module-local switch constants in the integration and mock crates, and any imports whose only purpose was to bring switch constants into scope.
rubrics.rationale: This case keeps its switches in a dedicated module plus module-local declarations; a resolution that leaves retired switches or their housing behind is inseparable from the pattern itself.

rubrics.criterion: Private helpers that only the removed branches ever called are removed with them: the message-count trim target in the conversation chain, the plain-text tool description renderer in the tools collection, the bounds computation in the token splitter, the provider-prefixed alias renderer on the model enum, the flat accounting helper in the ChatGPT token estimator, and the collapsed-role mapper in the ChatGPT prompt module all disappear rather than remaining as never-called code.
rubrics.rationale: Each disabled branch was given its own private helper, so the helpers exist solely at the removed branches' service; leaving them is the orphaned-reference failure this case is built to surface.

rubrics.criterion: Runtime-selected behavior is not deleted alongside the retired branches: the environment-variable trim-budget override in the conversation chain keeps functioning as operator-driven configuration, and runtime-dependent guards (message counts, emptiness of accumulated stream bodies) keep their sides.
rubrics.rationale: The conversation chain carries a genuine runtime selection adjacent to the retired one; misreading runtime-selectable paths as dead and removing them is the case-specific over-removal trap.

rubrics.criterion: No debris from the retired paths survives in the tree: no import of a deleted constant or helper remains, no emptied switch module file is kept with or without its module registration, and no leftover item from this cleanup draws a never-used report from the compiler.
rubrics.rationale: The injection added imports, a module, and a module registration purely to carry the retired stages; a sound equivalent repair must not leave fragments of that scaffolding, whatever its final file organization is.

rubrics.criterion: Internal signature details that existed only to serve the removed code are simplified away, such as the receiver mutability in the stream assembly function that only the removed segment-copying block required.
rubrics.rationale: Beyond bulk deletion, a careful cleanup notices incidental residue the conditionally-removed code caused; this distinguishes a thorough resolution from a mechanical one.

rubrics.criterion: Observable outcomes stay identical to the pre-change live behavior: model names render without provider prefixes, chat roles keep their distinct wire mapping, message token estimates keep the model-family overheads, the embeddings result is the untruncated requested vector, tool descriptions keep their machine-readable serialized structure, tool invocation extraction accepts the same YAML from the same model output, prompt combination yields the same chat/text shapes, text splitting yields the same chunk products, streamed replies assemble to the same data values, and conversation trimming still enforces the token budget.
rubrics.rationale: Each fix site doubles as a live behavior with visible output; these are the concrete regressions a hasty side-by-side deletion or a switch flip would produce in this codebase.

rubrics.criterion: The public API surface is untouched: no public type, trait, function, or constant is deleted, renamed, or de-published, and the deprecated model variants on the ChatGPT enum remain present; deprecation is retained-API, not dead code.
rubrics.rationale: This workspace carries a family of deprecated model variants that a legacy-themed cleanup would plausibly reach; removing genuine public API would break the compatibility boundary the task states.

rubrics.criterion: The retired paths are genuinely deleted rather than re-gated: no new configuration knob, Cargo feature, or fresh constant is introduced to keep the disabled implementations selectable.
rubrics.rationale: Converting a retired switch into a new feature flag is the tempting 'safe' non-resolution in this exact codebase, because the pattern is already dressed as toggles; it preserves the dead weight the task asks to remove.
